query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with 0.5 at% boron will refine its grain structure, strengthen grain boundaries, and thereby increase fracture toughness and ductility while preserving its magnetocaloric and barocaloric performance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 HEA exhibiting large caloric response but poor load-bearing integrity (fracture toughness ~5 MPa√m, elongation ~1%).
generation.intervention: Addition of 0.5 at% boron to the alloy melt followed by standard homogenization.
generation.conditions: Magnetic field 0→5 T, hydrostatic pressure 0→1 GPa, temperature range 230–350 K.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron segregation/precipitation at grain boundaries leading to grain refinement and crack‐path deflection.
generation.mechanism: B atoms decorate and strengthen grain boundaries, inhibiting crack initiation and propagation with minimal disruption of the martensitic transformation driving caloric effects.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fracture toughness K_IC increases by ≥20% and room-temperature ductility by ≥20% relative to baseline; magnetocaloric entropy change ΔS_m and barocaloric entropy change ΔS_b remain within ±10% of baseline values.
generation.baseline: Untreated alloy: K_IC ~5 MPa√m, compressive elongation ~1%, ΔS_m ~9 J/kg·K (0→5 T), ΔS_b ~7 J/kg·K (0→1 GPa).
generation.boundary: Valid for fields up to 5 T, pressures up to 1 GPa, temperatures 230–350 K.
generation.uncertainty: Medium; while boron is known to toughen steels and shape-memory alloys, its impact on this specific HEA’s caloric properties is extrapolated and untested.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two alloy batches (baseline and +0.5 at% B) by arc melting and homogenization. Measure fracture toughness (ASTM E399) and compressive ductility at ambient temperature. Measure ΔS_m under 0→5 T via DSC/magnetometry and ΔS_b under 0→1 GPa via pressure-DSC across 230–350 K.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if B doping yields <20% improvement in K_IC or ductility, or if ΔS_m or ΔS_b deviates by >10% from baseline.
